title: Python Encapsulation Quiz
description: Test your understanding of encapsulation in Python classes.

questions.question: What is encapsulation in Python?
options: Restricting access to some components of an object
questions.explanation: Encapsulation restricts direct access to object attributes and methods, usually by using private variables.

questions.question: Which prefix makes an attribute private in Python?
questions.explanation: Double underscore '__' before a variable name makes it private to the class.

questions.question: What is the main benefit of encapsulation?
options: Protecting object integrity by preventing direct modification of attributes
questions.explanation: Encapsulation ensures controlled access to attributes, maintaining object integrity.

questions.question: Which of the following is a valid way to access a private variable indirectly?
questions.explanation: Private variables are accessed indirectly via getter (and setter) methods.

questions.question: What does the term 'data hiding' refer to in Python?
options: Hiding internal object details using private attributes
questions.explanation: Data hiding protects the internal state of an object by restricting access to private attributes.

questions.question: Can private variables be accessed outside their class directly?
questions.explanation: Private variables cannot be accessed directly; you need methods like getters/setters.

questions.question: How do setter methods relate to encapsulation?
options: They provide controlled modification of private attributes
questions.explanation: Setter methods allow safe modification of private attributes while enforcing constraints.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about private methods in Python?
options: They are automatically executed at class load
They are not accessible outside the class directly
They can be called from any module freely
They are faster than public methods
questions.explanation: Private methods are meant to be used only inside the class and cannot be called directly from outside.

questions.question: Which of these demonstrates encapsulation?
options: def add(a, b): return a + b
questions.explanation: Using private attributes and getter methods in a class demonstrates encapsulation.

questions.question: What happens if you try to access a private variable directly?
questions.explanation: Direct access to private variables outside the class raises an AttributeError in Python.
